messages:
incident-bot: [P1] cluster gpu-prod-6 — repeated CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_FAILED + container restarts on runtime pods (3 nodes flapped in last 12m). Auto-escalate to eng-oncall. Trace: /alerts/1759876543
oncall-amber: ACK. I'm on it, pulling logs and recent deploys.
raj: seeing the same in runtime metrics — KV cache resident pages creeping steadily. Paging count + refcount ops spike ~6h ago.
sre-liz: node events show oom_kill for container "redwood-runtime" then kubelet restart. dmesg snippet: 
```
[  1234.567890] Out of memory: Killed process 12345 (redwood-runti) total-vm:210000kB, anon-rss:100000kB
[  1234.568112] cuda: out of memory while allocating 12582912 bytes
[  1234.568200] runtime allocator: slab_refcount_zero: panic at allocator.cc:482
```
taylor: infra shows 3 separate nodes rebooted within 10m window; autoscaler briefly spun up pods and they immediately OOM on attach. No recent infra changes.
support-jordan: Product reports 12 customers seeing 503s; some long-generation timeouts. I'm tracking customer list and affected routes.
oncall-amber: quick triage — pattern looks like slow-memory-creep in the paged-attention allocator + KV cache fragmentation causing a cascading slow OOM -> CUDA launch failures -> container crash. This matches a regression we saw in last runtime build (rollup 2024-11-08).
raj: confirming — graphs show KV_CACHE_ratio going from 0.45 -> 0.92 over ~8h for model /gpt-xlarge-paged. Also observed allocator slab fragmentation metric rising.
prod-ryan: is there an easy mitigation to stop new requests from aggravating? Can we flip a runtime flag to force non-paged attention or disable large KV cache allocations?
oncall-amber: yes. Plan A (fast): toggle ATTENTION_PAGING=disabled on the runtime deployment for the hot model and reduce max_batch_size -> route traffic to non-paged path (more CPU but avoids paging leak). Also set KV_CACHE_EVICT_THRESHOLD=0.6 to be aggressive.
raj: prepared patch. Commands: 
```
kubectl set env deployment/redwood-runtime ATTENTION_PAGING=false --namespace=prod
kubectl set env deployment/redwood-runtime KV_CACHE_EVICT_THRESHOLD=0.6 --namespace=prod
kubectl rollout restart deployment/redwood-runtime -n prod
```
raj: note — rollout will restart pods on affected nodes; that costs short-lived errors but should stop the slow creep.
stew-liz: also recommend bumping OOM score and enabling earlier eviction hooks, but that's more intrusive. For now, do the env flip and throttle batches.
support-jordan: will notify customers that we're applying mitigations and that we're working on a root cause. ETA message: "Applying emergency mitigation — may cause brief 503s while pods restart. We expect improved stability within 10-15m."
raj: executing now. Patching env + reducing MAX_BATCH=8.
raj: patch applied, rollout started. Watching logs.
(small gap)
raj: /logs show new pods coming up and not hitting immediate OOM. KV cache resident appears to plateau. No new CUDA launch failures in last 90s.
prod-ryan: nice. Any perf/latency impact?
noncall-amber: yes, latency for large generations will increase ~1.8x for affected model. Prioritize routing high-SLA customers to dedicated capacity or fallback quantized model.
support-jordan: updating status page and open tickets. Notifying top affected customers with suggested mitigations.
raj: one pod still OOM'ing occasionally — digging deeper, looks like a particular attention config (seq_len=8192) triggers larger KV allocations. Will add a targeted traffic cut for that tenant route.
sre-liz: infra: we should cordon the flappy nodes and drain to stop restarts during analysis. Command: 
```
kubectl cordon gpu-prod-6a
kubectl drain gpu-prod-6a --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```
taylor: cordoned and drained 6a and 6c. Autoscaler will replace capacity if needed.
noncall-amber: next steps: 1) keep ATTENTION_PAGING disabled for hot model for now, 2) aggressive eviction set, 3) route heavy seq_len customers off the paged model, 4) collect heap/kv snapshots from one stable pod for postmortem, 5) prepare rollback to prior runtime binary (sha: a1b2c3d) if regression confirmed.
raj: capturing heap snapshot with kv-metrics tool now: `./kv-dump --out /tmp/kv-1759876543.snap`
prod-ryan: flagging for oncall-night — handoff message includes mitigation steps, links to metrics, and customer impact summary.
noncall-amber: handoff -> oncall-night (taylor) at 23:00 PST. Current state: mitigations applied, observable plateau in KV resident, reduced CUDA errors, some latency degradation, customers being notified.
support-jordan: customers patched with advice: reduce seq_len or use dedicated concurrency. I'll attach list to the incident ticket.
raj: logging runbook entry: https://confluence/redwood/runbooks/allocator-heisenbug (temp)
noncall-amber: leaving detailed notes in the incident ticket and assigning to runtime-team for root cause. If night-oncall sees reappearance, escalate to escalations-channel and consider emergency rollback to runtime a1b2c3d.
prod-ryan: thanks all. Passing to night oncall — be ready to run quick rollback if we see reacceleration.
(t+9m) incident-bot: Mitigation check: top-level alert suppressed after stabilization observed for 5m. Continue monitoring.
